title: Newly Declassified Pentagon Documents Suggest Popular California Tourist Spot Was Once Hub for UFO Sightings
excerpt: The reports include “flying saucers” and a “purplish-white” object hovering in the sky over Catalina Island
content:
Toria Sheffield

Sat, October 31, 2026 at 9:00 AM UTC

NEED TO KNOW

  • Newly released Pentagon documents detail four alleged UFO sightings over California’s Catalina Island between 1949 and 1955

  • Witnesses reported seeing mysterious objects in the sky, including silver “flying saucers” and a bright orange object

  • The documents were released on Oct. 23 as part of an ongoing federal initiative to make government records related to UFO sightings and investigations publicly accessible

Newly released documents from the Pentagon reveal that California’s Catalina Island was once a hot spot for alleged UFO sightings.

The Department of Defense released 28 files involving unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAPs) — also known as UFOs — in an online drop on Friday, Oct. 23. The files were released as part of a federal initiative launched in May to make government records about UFO sightings and investigations publicly available.

Four of the 28 files involved sightings specifically on Catalina Island, a popular tourist destination located about 22 miles off the coast of Southern California, in the 1940s and 1950s, according to the Los Angeles Times. 

The first alleged sighting was reported by a man named Percy Wackey, who lived in Avalon — the island’s only incorporated city — in May 1949.

Wackey claimed that his wife and an unnamed individual saw six objects over the island on April 28, 1949.

Another sighting in August 1952 involved three Boy Scouts who claimed they saw silver “flying saucers” flying faster than a jet plane.

In November 1953, a man said he saw a “purplish-white” object hovering in place over the island before heading toward Los Angeles, which is located about 50 miles east.

The fourth and final sighting occurred in Avalon in March 1955, when a man named Paul J. Carr reported seeing a bright orange object “the size of a nickel held at arm’s length” fall “straight down” toward the island.

While speaking to CBS News about the reports, Bill Diamond, the president and CEO of the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence Institute, said that while it is statistically probable that life exists elsewhere in the universe, most reports of UFO sightings on Earth merit a healthy dose of skepticism.

“It’s hard to imagine coming all this way and then flying by for a couple of hours and then leaving,” he told the outlet.

He additionally noted that the reports dropped in the most recent tranche of files were from a time when science fiction and space exploration gripped the public consciousness and imagination.

“There are more pictures of UFOs from that period than there are now, and we have literally billions of very capable high-resolution cameras in the hands of people all over the world,” he said.

The Department of Defense has released a total of 478 files across seven drops since launching the new initiative, per the L.A. Times.
